about: The houses of trial of Xibalba are named one by one: after the Dark House come Xuxulim Ha, full of cold; the Jaguar House, where jaguars are shut in; the Bat House, full of shrieking bats with no way out; and the fifth, the House of Blades. Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu are not put through them. When the brothers come before Huncame and Vucub Came, the lords ask for the torch and the cigar given them in the Dark House, and they have used them up. Today your days are over, say the lords, and the brothers are sacrificed and buried at Pucbal Chah. Hunhunahpu's head is cut off and set in the branches of a tree by the road, and at once the tree, which had borne no fruit before, is covered with fruit: the calabash, still called ‘the head of Hunhunahpu’. The head can no longer be told from the fruit. The lords marvel at it, and all Xibalba forbids anyone to go near the tree. But a maiden hears the story, and her coming is told next.

sentences.t: Are v nabe ri Queꜫuma Ha, vtuquel queꜫum vpam.
sentences.l: This its first the Dark House, alone darkness its-inside.
sentences.i: The first was the Dark House, with nothing but darkness inside.
sentences.n: The houses of trial of Xibalba, which the last part ended by calling many, are now named one by one. Are v nabe 'this (is) its first': v- 'its' + nabe 'first', the first of the trials (MS arevnabe, divided by us). Queꜫuma Ha 'Dark House' is the house where the brothers spent the night at the end of the last part (toggle Q'equma Ja). vtuquel queꜫum vpam 'only darkness its inside': vtuquel 'by itself, alone' gives 'nothing but', as in the last part. This paragraph and the next three are a list, each house with its number, its name and what is inside it.

sentences.t: Vcab chicut Xuxulim Ha vbi; ꜩaꜩ chi teu vpam, zac xuruxuh, cac caracoh chi xurulah teu choc vloc chupam.
sentences.l: Its-second again-then Xuxulim House its-name; thick with cold its-inside, white xuruxuh(?), cac(?) caracoh(?) that xurulah(?) cold it-enters hither inside.
sentences.i: The second was named Xuxulim Ha: inside it was thick with cold, white and rattling (?), and the cold came whistling (?) in.
sentences.n: Vcab 'its second': v- + cab 'two'. Xuxulim Ha is kept as a name; Brasseur's note takes xuxulim as 'the north wind, or the shivering of the north wind' ('la bise ou le frémissement du vent du nord'), and the text itself says what is inside: ꜩaꜩ chi teu vpam 'thick with cold its inside' (ꜩaꜩ 'many, thick'; teu 'cold', toggle tew). xuruxuh, caracoh and xurulah are not otherwise known; each repeats its sounds (xu-ru-xuh, ca-ra-coh, xu-ru-lah) and they look like sound words for the wind. 'Rattling' and 'whistling' are guesses; Brasseur renders the whole as 'a piercing wind, a cold and unbearable wind that filled everything within'. cac caracoh is a doubtful reading: the manuscript clearly has c, not the z of zac xuruxuh in the line before, where Brasseur reads zak (zakcaracoh), 'white' again. Whether cac is a word (in earlier parts it was unexplained, or fire) or a slip for zac is not known; it is left out of the English, and the toggle respells the letters. choc vloc chupam 'it comes in, hither, inside': ch- + oc 'enter', as in the last part.

sentences.t: Rox chicut Balami Ha vbi, vtuquel balam ꜭo chupan;
sentences.l: Its-third again-then Jaguar House its-name, alone jaguar there-is inside;
sentences.i: The third was named the Jaguar House: there was nothing in it but jaguars;
sentences.n: Rox 'its third': r- 'its' (the form before a vowel) + ox 'three'. Balami Ha: balam 'jaguar' + -i + ha 'house'. As a description it is translated, like the Dark House (Brasseur 'la maison des Tigres'; toggle B'alami Ja). balam ꜭo chupan 'jaguar there is inside': the noun is singular for the kind, as tucur 'owl' was in the last part. chupan is written with n here (MS chu|pan; Brasseur chupam), as in earlier parts; the toggle gives chupam.

sentences.t: que quichouic, que buchuvic chi matat, que chi qui tit; que e ꜩapim balam pa ha.
sentences.l: they quichouic(?), they crowd with matat(?), they chi qui tit(?); thus they(-are) shut-in jaguars in house.
sentences.i: they milled about (?), they crowded together fiercely (?), they bared their teeth (?): jaguars shut up in the house.
sentences.n: Three short clauses with que, c- (ongoing) + e 'they' (toggle ke), say what the jaguars kept doing; none of the verbs is clear. quichouic is read with Brasseur ('they mingled'), so 'milled about' (inferred; MS quichouic with u, as he has it). buchuvic 'crowd together', as in an earlier part (inferred, after Brasseur). chi matat is not otherwise known; 'fiercely' follows Brasseur's 'with a fierce air' (a guess). que chi qui tit is a doubtful reading: the manuscript has chiquiht, and in this hand t and h are both tall and hard to tell apart (vtihobal is written like vhhobal); it is read qui tit with Brasseur, who seems to render it 'grinning'. qui may be 'their'; tit is not known, and 'bared their teeth' is a guess. que e ꜩapim balam 'so they (are) shut in, jaguars': ꜩapim is taken as a participle of ꜩap 'shut, close' (Brasseur 'enfermés'); the modern word is tz'apij, so the toggle gives tz'apim (inferred). pa ha 'in the house'.

sentences.t: Ꜩoꜩi Ha vbi vcah vtihobal;
sentences.l: Bat House its-name its-fourth its-trial;
sentences.i: The fourth trial was named the Bat House;
sentences.n: ꜩoꜩ is the bat (Brasseur zotz, 'chauves-souris'); Ꜩoꜩi Ha is built like Balami Ha, noun + -i + ha 'house', and is translated likewise. The manuscript writes the looped tz ligature at both ends of the word, here and in ꜩoꜩ twice below (the establisher compared it with the plain z), where the modern word for the bat is sotz'. The toggle respells the letters (Tzotzi, tzotz), since the modern spelling of Ximénez's form is not certain. vcah 'its fourth' (cah 'four'). vtihobal 'its trial', as in the last part (tih 'try, test' + -obal).

sentences.t: vtuquel ꜩoꜩ vpam chi ha, que ꜩiꜩotic, que ꜩitilahic, que ropop pa ha, e ꜩapin ꜩoꜩ, mahabi que el vi.
sentences.l: alone bat its-inside of house, they shriek(?), they flutter(?), they fly-about(?) in house, they(-are) shut-in bats, not-there-is they go-out there.
sentences.i: inside the house there was nothing but bats; they shrieked (?), they fluttered (?), they flew about (?) in the house, bats shut in with no way out.
sentences.n: vtuquel ꜩoꜩ vpam chi ha 'only bats its inside, of the house', the frame used for the Dark House. Three clauses with que (c- + e 'they'). ꜩiꜩotic and ꜩitilahic look like sound words: 'shriek' and 'flutter' follow Brasseur ('crying, beating their wings'), guesses. Both are doubtful readings: the manuscript has ꜩiꜩohic and ꜩih'lahic, with the same t/h doubt as qui tit above, decided with Brasseur (tzitzotic, tzitilahic). ropop 'fly about' follows Brasseur's 'voltigeant' (inferred; toggle by the letters). e ꜩapin ꜩoꜩ 'they (are) shut in, bats': ꜩapin is written with n here, where the jaguars' line has ꜩapim with m; both are printed as written and taken as the same word (toggle tz'apin). mahabi que el vi 'there is no going out for them': mahabi 'there is not' + que el 'they go out' + vi 'from there'.

sentences.t: Roo chicut Chaim Ha vbi, vtuquel chaꜫol chupam, zac leloh re chi cha, chi ꜩininic, chi yohohic chiri pa ha.
sentences.l: Its-fifth again-then Blade House its-name, alone chaꜫol(?) inside, white leloh(?) its-teeth(?) of blade, ꜩininic(?), yohohic(?) there in house.
sentences.i: The fifth was named the House of Blades (?): inside there was nothing but chaq'ol (?), white and gleaming (?) at the edges of the blades, clashing (?), grinding (?) there in the house.
sentences.n: Roo 'its fifth' (Brasseur Roo): r- 'its' + o(o), taken as 'five' from its place in the list (inferred); the form is not otherwise known and the toggle respells the letters. The first letter is Ximénez's r, which can look like v. Chaim Ha: cha is the obsidian blade or arrow point (Brasseur's note on cha at the torch in the last part: the arrow and the arrow point, obsidian or flint; in his introduction chay is obsidian or the lance, and he names this house Chaim-ha, 'la Maison des Lances d'Obsidienne'; his text here Chayim-ha) + -im + ha 'house'; 'House of Blades' is inferred (Brasseur's French here renders 'house of the fighters'). chaꜫol is a doubtful reading: a q-shaped letter, taken as the tresillo, with an ink blot on the next letter that may hide another; Brasseur reads chakol (his k is plain q, so he does not support the tresillo) and renders 'victors', as if from the chac 'beat' of earlier parts. Its meaning is not known, and it is left in K'iche' in the English. zac leloh re is divided by us (MS ʒaclelohre, Brasseur zaklelohre undivided), a doubtful division: zac 'white'; leloh is not otherwise known ('gleaming' is a guess); re is taken as 'its teeth', the edge (inferred; it may be re 'of'); chi cha 'of blade'. ꜩininic and yohohic, each after chi, look like sound words; 'clashing' and 'grinding' are guesses (Brasseur has the fighters by turns resting and fighting). chiri pa ha 'there in the house'.

sentences.t: Que nabec vtihobal Xibalba.
sentences.l: Thus first its-trials Xibalba.
sentences.i: These were the first trials of Xibalba.
sentences.n: Que 'thus, such' (toggle Ke): 'such (were) the first trials of Xibalba'. The manuscript has que with a blot over the e; Brasseur reads Qui. nabec 'first, at first' (nabe + -c, toggle nab'ek). Brasseur's note thinks the houses of trial were nine in all.

sentences.t: Ma cu xe oc ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu chupam; xa vbixic apon oc vtihobal ha.
sentences.l: Not then they-entered the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu inside; only its-being-told arriving (oc) its-trial house.
sentences.i: But Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu did not go into them; the houses of trial are only named here (?).
sentences.n: Ma cu 'but not'. xe oc 'they entered'; chupam 'inside (them)'. Between Hunahpu and chupam the manuscript has a word struck through by Ximénez (it looks like xe); it is not printed. xa vbixic apon oc vtihobal ha 'only its being told reaches there, the houses of trial': vbixic 'its being said' (bih 'say' + passive -x + -ic), apon oc 'arriving there' (toggle oq). Brasseur reads xa u bixic apon-oc a bi tihobal ha, with a bi 'its name', which the manuscript does not have, and renders 'it sufficed to mention the names of these houses of trial'. The line is read as the narrator's remark that the houses are only named, since the brothers never entered them (inferred).

sentences.t: Ta xe oc cu apan oc Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu chuvach Huncame, Vvcub Came:
sentences.l: Then they-entered then away (oc) Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu before-the-face-of Huncame, Vvcub Came:
sentences.i: Then Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu came in before Huncame and Vucub Came:
sentences.n: The story goes back to the brothers after their night in the Dark House. xe oc … apan oc 'they went in there': oc 'enter', then apan 'away, there' with oc, the ending of direction (toggle ok … apan oq). chuvach 'before the face of': chi + v- 'his' + vach 'face'. The speaker of the next line is not named; Brasseur makes it the lords.

sentences.t: “Apa ꜭo vi ri nu zic? Aon ꜭo vi ri nu chah xhe yaoc chivech?” Xquec xvꜭhax cut.
sentences.l: “Where is there the my cigar? Aon(?) is there the my torch xhe(?) to-be-given to-you?” Xquec(?) were-told then.
sentences.i: “Where is my cigar? And where is my torch that was given to you?” they were asked.
sentences.n: Apa ꜭo vi 'where is it': apa 'where', ꜭo 'there is', vi pointing to the place. nu zic, nu chah 'my cigar', 'my torch' (nu- 'my'; toggle sik', chaj): the torch and the cigars given to the brothers in the Dark House, to be returned whole at dawn. Aon is not otherwise known; it is read 'where' with Brasseur, who repeats 'where' here, perhaps a form of apa (inferred; toggle by the letters). xhe yaoc 'that was given' (MS xheyaoc): Brasseur reads x-be ya-oc, 'that went to be given', the xbe … yaoc of the last part (his French 'qu'on vous a apportés la nuit dernière'); the manuscript has h, and xhe is printed as written (doubtful; toggle xje by the letters). chivech 'to you (pl.)'. Xquec xvꜭhax cut: Xquec is clear in its letters (MS xquec, read at 2×) but is not understood, and Brasseur does not print it as a word; it is left out of the English (toggle Xkek by the letters). xvꜭhax 'were spoken to': x- + vꜭhax (ꜭha 'speak' + passive -x), as xe vꜭhax 'they were told' in the last part, here without the plural e.

sentences.t: “Xca quizo, at ahau.”
sentences.l: “We-finished-it, you lord.”
sentences.i: “We have used them up, lord.”
sentences.n: Xca quizo 'we finished it': x- + ca- 'we' + quiz 'finish, end' + -o, the ending of a transitive verb at the end of its clause (as rilo 'he sees it'). quiz is the verb of the last part's xqui quiz 'they used up' (toggle k'iso; Brasseur ka qizo). at ahau 'you, lord'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala. Vacamic bala xquiz iꜫih.
sentences.l: “Good bala. Now bala it-ended your-day.
sentences.i: “Very well. Today, then, your days are over.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well', as in the house table; the second bala strengthens vacamic 'now, today' (inferred, as in earlier parts). xquiz iꜫih 'your day is finished': xquiz, the verb of the line before; iꜫih is i- 'your (pl.)' + ꜫih 'day, sun' (MS like iqeih, the q-shaped letter read as the tresillo; Brasseur x-qiz y gih). The day is the span of their life, perhaps their lot (inferred).

sentences.t: Quix camic, xqui zachic, xqui ca cup puch.
sentences.l: You-die, xqui(?) are-lost, xqui(?) ca are-cut-open(?) also.
sentences.i: You shall die, you shall be lost, and you shall be cut open (?).
sentences.n: Three lines in a row. Quix camic 'you (pl.) die': c- (ongoing) + ix 'you (pl.)' + cam 'die' + -ic. xqui zachic and xqui ca cup are taken as the same person, 'you', as the parallel requires and as Brasseur reads them (x-qu'y zachic, x-qu'y ca cup: 'you shall be destroyed, you shall be cut (in the chest)'). But the manuscript has xquiʒachic, xquica cup, with no x after qui where Quix camic has one, and xqui looks like the completive x- + qui- 'they'. Printed as written; a doubtful reading (toggle xki by the letters). zachic 'be lost, undone' (zach + -ic). cup is not otherwise known; 'cut open' is a guess after Brasseur (toggle kup). ca is left unrendered, as in earlier parts. puch 'also' tags the last of the three.

sentences.t: Varal xchi vevah vi ivach.
sentences.l: Here shall it-hide(?) there your-face.
sentences.i: Here your faces shall be hidden away (?).
sentences.n: MS xchivevah, divided as in the last part (xchi- 'shall', written apart). vevah is taken as eu 'hide' + -ah, the eu of euaxibal 'the place of hiding' in the first part, with a v- before it, perhaps v- 'it' (inferred; toggle wewaj by the letters). Brasseur reads x-ch'yv'euah, with iv- 'your (pl.)', and renders 'your memory shall remain buried in these places'. ivach 'your (pl.) face': i- + vach. vi 'there' points back to varal 'here'.

sentences.t: Quix puzic,” xꜭha Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.l: You-are-sacrificed,” he-said Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.i: You shall be sacrificed,” said Huncame and Vucub Came.
sentences.n: Quix puzic 'you (pl.) are sacrificed': c- + ix 'you (pl.)' + puz + -ic. puz was read 'sacrifice' in the last part (que ca puzu 'we sacrifice them'); its sense is not fully certain (inferred; Brasseur 'vous serez sacrifiés'; toggle pusik). xꜭha 'he said' is singular before the pair of names.

sentences.t: Ta xe puz cut, xe muc cut chi Pucbal Chah vbi; xe muc vi.
sentences.l: Then they-were-sacrificed then, they-were-buried then at Pucbal Chah its-name; they-were-buried there.
sentences.i: So they were sacrificed, and they were buried at the place called Pucbal Chah; there they were buried.
sentences.n: xe puz 'they were sacrificed'; xe muc 'they were buried' (muc 'bury', toggle muq, as in an earlier part). Pucbal Chah is kept as a place name. Brasseur renders it 'the Ash-heap', 'the place where ashes are put down, where they are thrown': chah would then be 'ash' (Brasseur's note on cha in the last part gives chaah, with two a, as 'ash'), and pucbal a place noun in -bal (inferred); by the letters chah is the torch of the last part (toggle Pukb'al Chaj). xe muc vi 'they were buried there' (MS xemucvi) repeats the verb; Brasseur leaves it out.

sentences.t: Xcat vholom ri Hunhunahpu; xa vnimal xmuquic ruꜭ ri vchac.
sentences.l: It-was-cut his-head the Hunhunahpu; only his-elder was-buried with the his-younger-brother.
sentences.i: Hunhunahpu's head was cut off; only the body of the elder was buried with his younger brother.
sentences.n: Xcat 'it was cut' has plain c, where Brasseur reads x-gat (his g is ꜫ) and renders 'they cut off the head'. It is taken as ꜫat 'cut', the cat of catol ꜩih 'the cutters of the word', the judges, in an earlier part (toggle xq'at, as q'atol there); it is not the cat 'burn' of the last part, though the letters are the same. vholom 'his head'. vnimal 'his elder (brother)': nim 'great' + -al. vchac 'his younger brother' (Brasseur u chag, his g is ꜫ; 'son jeune frère') is set against it; the toggle gives uchaq', the modern word, where the vchac 'its work' of an earlier part is uchak. xa vnimal 'only the elder' is taken as his body without the head (inferred; Brasseur 'the body of the elder'). xmuquic 'was buried' (muc + -ic).

sentences.t: “Chi ya ri vholom xol che ri tiquil pa be,” xꜭha cut Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.l: “Let give the his-head among tree the planted on road,” he-said then Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.i: “Put his head among the branches of the tree that stands by the road,” said Huncame and Vucub Came.
sentences.n: Chi ya 'let (them) put': chi (optative) + ya 'give, put'. xol che 'among the tree', in its branches (xol 'between, among'). tiquil 'planted, standing': tic 'plant', as in the first part's xchicatiquiba 'we shall plant', + -il (inferred; toggle tikil; Brasseur 'the tree that is in the middle of the road'). pa be 'on, by the road'.

sentences.t: Ta xbe cu yaoc vholom xol che.
sentences.l: Then it-went then to-be-given his-head among tree.
sentences.i: So his head was taken and set among the branches.
sentences.n: xbe … yaoc 'it went to be given': be 'go' + ya 'give' + -oc, as in the last part.

sentences.t: Ta xvachin curi che; mahabi vvach maha choco ri vholom ri Hunhunahpu chuxol che.
sentences.l: Then it-bore-fruit then tree; there-was-not its-fruit not-yet it-entered the his-head the Hunhunahpu among tree.
sentences.i: Then the tree bore fruit; it had had no fruit before the head of Hunhunahpu was put among its branches.
sentences.n: xvachin 'it bore fruit': vach 'face, fruit' (the fruit is the face a tree shows) + -in, made a verb (inferred; Brasseur 'se couvrit aussitôt de fruits'; toggle xwachin). curi 'then' (MS curi che, joined as in the last part). mahabi vvach 'there was no fruit on it'. maha choco 'before it went in': maha 'not yet' + ch- + oc 'enter' + -o (inferred; toggle choko by the letters). chuxol 'in among': chi + v- 'its' + xol.

sentences.t: Are curi zima cohcha chire vacamic “vholom Hunhunahpu” chuꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: This then calabash we-say to-it now “his-head Hunhunahpu” it-is-called.
sentences.i: This is the calabash, which we still call today ‘the head of Hunhunahpu’, as it is said.
sentences.n: zima is the calabash tree and its round fruit (Brasseur's note: 'the calabash tree, called tzima in Quiché'; his text prints tzima). The manuscript writes it with the plain z, without the loop of the tz ligature (the establisher compared it at 2× with Ꜩoꜩi on the same page), here and twice more in this part. The word is presumably tz'ima', but the toggle respells the letter as written (sima), as it did for the last part's zimah (simaj) and ziban (sib'an), whose modern words also have tz'. cohcha 'we say': c- + oh 'we' + cha 'say' (Brasseur koh cha; toggle kojcha). chire 'to it'. vacamic 'now, today': the writers' own time. chuꜭhaxic 'as it is said'. The quotation marks are ours.

sentences.t: Ta xumaihah cut Huncame, Vvcub Came vvach ri che; humah colocac vvach.
sentences.l: Then he-marvelled-at then Huncame, Vvcub Came its-fruit the tree; all(?) round its-fruit.
sentences.i: Huncame and Vucub Came marvelled at the fruit of the tree; every fruit was round (?).
sentences.n: xumaihah 'he marvelled at it': x- + v- 'he' + maihah 'marvel at' (inferred, as in earlier parts), singular like xꜭha above. humah colocac vvach is read with Brasseur, 'the fruit was round all over alike': humah, 'some' in an earlier part, is here taken as 'all alike' (inferred); colocac 'round' may be the coloquic 'round' of the last part (a guess; Brasseur colocak). The toggle respells colocac by the letters.

sentences.t: Ma cu calah ꜭo chi vi ri vholom Hunhunahpu; xa hunam chic vvach ruꜭ vvach zima.
sentences.l: Not then clear is any-more there the his-head Hunhunahpu; only alike now its-face with its-fruit calabash.
sentences.i: Where the head of Hunhunahpu was could no longer be seen; its face was now the same as the fruit of the calabash.
sentences.n: Ma … calah 'it is not clear, not to be seen' (toggle q'alaj). ꜭo chi vi 'is any longer there': chi is taken as chic 'any more', its c not written (toggle chik). hunam 'equal, alike': hun 'one' + -am (inferred; Brasseur 'of the same kind'; toggle junam). The two vvach play on the word: the head's face and the tree's fruit. zima again with the plain z (toggle sima, as above).

sentences.t: Cu rilo ronohel Xibalba ta chul qui caiih.
sentences.l: Then he-sees-it all Xibalba when come-here they-look(?).
sentences.i: All Xibalba saw it, when they came to look at it.
sentences.n: rilo 'he sees it': r- + il 'see' + -o, singular with ronohel Xibalba 'all Xibalba'. chul 'come here' (ch- + vl). qui caiih 'they look at it' is inferred, with Brasseur's qui cayih ('when they went to look at it'). The manuscript has quicaiih, with no descender for a y: a doubtful reading, and the toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: Nim vꜭoheic ri che xux chi qui ꜭux, rumal huzu xubanic, ta xoc vholom Hunhunahpu chuxol.
sentences.l: Great its-being the tree it-became in their heart, because suddenly it-was-done, when it-entered his-head Hunhunahpu among-it.
sentences.i: In their hearts the tree became a great thing, because of what had happened so suddenly when Hunhunahpu's head was put among its branches.
sentences.n: Nim vꜭoheic ri che 'great (was) the being of the tree': vꜭoheic, ꜭohe 'be' + -ic, as in an earlier part. xux 'it became' (x- + ux). chi qui ꜭux 'in their hearts': the q-shaped letter is read ꜭ (MS qux), as in the last two parts. huzu 'suddenly' (toggle jusuk, as in earlier parts). xubanic: x- + v- + ban 'do' + -ic, 'it was done', it happened (inferred).

sentences.t: Xeꜭha curi Xibalba chi quibil quib: “Ma co ma chupuvic ri vvach; ma co naipu ma oc apan oc chuxe che,” xeꜭha;
sentences.l: They-said then Xibalba among themselves: “Not there-be not chupuvic(?) the its-fruit; not there-be likewise not enter away (oc) at-the-foot tree,” they-said;
sentences.i: Then Xibalba said among themselves: “Let no one pick (?) its fruit; let no one go in under the tree either,” they said;
sentences.n: chi quibil quib 'among themselves'. A couplet: Ma co ma …, ma co naipu ma … 'let there not be (one who) …': ma 'not' + co 'there is' (ꜭo with plain c; Brasseur qo; toggle k'o), and ma again before the verb, read together as 'let no one …' (inferred). chupuvic is not otherwise known (perhaps ch- + upuv + -ic); 'pick' is a guess from the context. Brasseur reads ri a vach, 'your face', where the manuscript has ri vvach, and renders only the second line ('let there be no one bold enough to sit at the foot of the tree'). naipu 'likewise', nai + pu (toggle naypu, as naipuch is naypuch). ma oc apan oc 'not go in there' (oc 'enter', then oc of direction). chuxe che 'at the foot of the tree' (chi + v- 'its' + xe 'root, foot'). The manuscript runs the words together (maco machupuvic, maco naipu maoc apanoc); the division is ours.

sentences.t: xqui catah quib, xqui quil quib Xibalba conohel.
sentences.l: they-forbade(?) themselves, they-held-back(?) themselves Xibalba all.
sentences.i: all Xibalba forbade it to one another and held one another back (?).
sentences.n: A couplet: xqui catah quib, xqui quil quib 'they … one another, they … one another' (quib 'themselves, one another'). Both verbs are read after Brasseur ('forbidding one another and defending themselves'): catah 'forbid' and quil 'hold back' are inferred. quil has plain c where Brasseur reads gil (his g is ꜫ); the toggle respells both by the letters.

sentences.t: Ma cu calah chi ri vholom Hunhunahpu; xa hunamatal chic ruc vvach che, ri zima vbi xuxic.
sentences.l: Not then clear any-more the his-head Hunhunahpu; only made-alike now with its-fruit tree, the calabash its-name it-became.
sentences.i: The head of Hunhunahpu could no longer be seen; it had become one with the fruit of the tree, which came to be named the calabash.
sentences.n: The narrator repeats what ¶10 said and closes the episode. chi 'any more' (chic, as above). hunamatal 'made alike, one with': hunam 'alike' + -atal, a participle of state (inferred; toggle junamatal). ruc 'with' has plain c in the manuscript, where ruꜭ in ¶10 has the g; it is the same word (toggle ruk', as in earlier parts). ri zima vbi xuxic 'whose name became zima': xuxic 'it became' (ux + -ic). zima again with the plain z (toggle sima).

sentences.t: Nim cut vꜩihoxic xuta hun capoh.
sentences.l: Great then its-telling she-heard a maiden.
sentences.i: And a maiden heard this great tale.
sentences.n: vꜩihoxic 'its telling', a passive made a noun, as in the first part. xuta 'she heard it': x- + v- 'she' + ta 'hear'. hun capoh 'a maiden', in lower case: she is not yet named. capoh has plain c where Brasseur reads gapoh (his g is ꜫ); the modern word is q'apoj 'young woman', so the toggle restores q' (inferred).

sentences.t: Va cute xchi ca biyh roponic.
sentences.l: This then shall we-tell her-arrival.
sentences.i: Now we shall tell of her coming.
sentences.n: Va cute 'this, then' (MS vacute; Brasseur va cate). xchi ca biyh 'we shall tell': xchi- 'shall' + ca- 'we' (plain c; Brasseur ka; toggle qa) + biyh 'say, tell', as in earlier parts. roponic 'her arriving there': r- 'her' + opon + -ic. In the manuscript the next line is Ximénez's indented heading for the maiden's story, which begins the next part.
